newsitem.title: UK: Bristol says study shows Zerit better against HIV.
newsitem.headline: Bristol says study shows Zerit better against HIV.

text.p: Bristol-Myers Squibb Co said on Tuesday that trials had shown double combination therapy using its Zerit (stavudine) drug worked better than those using Glaxo Wellcome's standard AZT (retrovir).
With more than a dozen different drugs on the market, doctors are keen for information on which combination works best.

Bristol researchers told a symposium organised by the company in Cannes, France that tests on using either Zerit or AZT with Glaxo's Epivir (3TC or lamivudine) showed the Zerit combination worked better.

Dr Juergen Poppinger of the Curatorium for Immunodeficiency in Munich tested the combinations on 67 patients who had not been given drugs before and found after 26 weeks those on Zerit and Epivir had lower levels of virus in their blood and more infection-fighting CD4 cells.
Most trials have shown that adding a third drug, a protease inhibitor, gives the best effects.

Dr Schlomo Staszewski of the Goethe University Clinic in Frankfurt said that giving patients Zerit, Epivir and Merck's Crixivan (indinavir) protease inhibitor, or Zerit, Bristol's Videx (ddI) and Crixivan reduced the virus in the blood by up to 99 percent.
"Overall, after 24 weeks of therapy, 53 percent of patients experienced a reduction of HIV in the blood below the limit of detection," Bristol said in a statement released in London.
Other tests showed that resistance to Zerit was rare, Bristol said.

In a second release, Merck said that research announced at a conference in Sao Paulo that people using Crixivan alone were two-thirds less likely to develop an opportunistic infection, cancer, or to die than those using AZT alone.
Those using Crixivan with AZT saw a 70 percent reduction in likelihood of infection, cancer or death while those on Crixivan alone had a 61 percent reduction.
The 996 patients in the Brazil trial, which started in April 1995, would now all be offered Crixivan for free, Merck said. -- Maggie Fox, London Newsroom, 44-171-542-8958
